summary: Conflicting group-derived roles prevent access to Support Tool (403 despite SCIM membership)
description: Issue summary: Several engineers report receiving 403 Forbidden when opening the internal Support Tool immediately after an IdP (Okta) identity merge for users who have overlapping group memberships. Impact: Affected users cannot access the Support Tool to triage customer tickets. This blocks oncall and daily support workflows for a subset of staff.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Ensure user has two Okta profiles recently merged (externalId collision) via SCIM merge job.
2) User signs in to console -> SSO redirect to identity-proxy -> token exchange completes.
3) Visit /support-tool and observe 403 response from rbac-service despite expected group claims present in token.
actual_result: 403 Forbidden returned by rbac-service; support tool shows 'You do not have permission to view this page.'
expected_result: Users with group 'support-team' should receive role 'support_agent' and access Support Tool.
logs: 2026-03-12T09:42:21Z rbac-service WARN role-resolve user=uid:1234 resolved_roles=[support_agent:null, eng_read:true] note='shadowed by stale-mapping'
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: SCIM merge left a stale group mapping entry in the legacy-group-mapper table which causes a null role binding during evaluation.
Observed that token includes both 'support-team' and 'support-team-legacy' claims; rbac-service treats 'support-team-legacy' as a deny-mapping in the conflict-resolution logic.
Checked provisioning logs for SCIM merge job run on 2026-03-11: /ops/scim-merge-job/2026-03-11. Exit code 0 but warnings about duplicate externalId were present.
Replayed the role resolution function locally with the same token and confirmed conflict-resolution returns empty binding when a deny-tagged legacy group coexists with allow-tagged modern group.
Reproduction only occurs for users whose SCIM profile had both group aliases during merge; newly-provisioned single-profile users unaffected.
Related historical incident: INT-472001 (intermittent-403-on-access-request-due-to-session-affinity-cache-eviction) observed similar symptom but different root cause (session affinity).
comments: Priya Nair (Support): Reported initial customer-facing impact and attached two user tokens and timestamps.
Evan Chen (SRE): Confirmed rbac-service logs show conflict resolution returning no effective role for uid:1234. Added temporary logging and increased log-level for role-eval module.
Diego Morales (Identity): Ran SCIM merge job replay in staging and reproduced stale-legacy-group artifact. Proposed quick mitigation: mark legacy-group prefixes as benign in conflict logic.
Aisha Patel (Product Ops): Requested risk assessment for changing conflict-resolution rules and requested a rollback plan.
mitigation_attempts: 1) Short-term: SRE toggled rbac-service config to prefer allow-mappings over deny for groups with legacy prefixes for 2 hours (hotfix), which restored access for confirmed users.
2) Re-provisioning affected users (force SCIM sync) also fixes the issue but is manual and not scalable.
root_cause: SCIM identity merge left coexisting legacy and canonical group claims. RBAC conflict-resolution logic treated legacy group as deny due to historical mapping; when both claims are present resolution returned no effective role.
resolution: Deployed a targeted config change to the rbac-service conflict-resolution to treat legacy group aliases as neutral if a canonical allow mapping exists. Hotfix rolled out to prod us-east on 2026-03-13 03:20Z. Follow-on change scheduled: database cleanup job to remove legacy-group mappings during SCIM merges and add CI check to merge job to prevent duplicate group aliases.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-13 03:20Z - hotfix config applied by Evan Chen; access restored for confirmed users.
2026-03-14 - scheduled runbook update to include SCIM merge verification steps (assigned Diego Morales).
follow_up_actions: 1) Implement DB cleanup as part of SCIM merge pipeline - owner: Identity team - target 2026-03-20.
2) Add unit tests for conflict-resolution logic covering legacy+canonical groups - owner: SRE - target 2026-03-17.
3) Update oncall runbook with immediate mitigation steps (hotfix toggle) - owner: Support - target 2026-03-16.
notes_for_postmortem: Issue qualifies for follow-up in weekly ops review due to customer-impacting access outage for internal support. Include timeline of SCIM merge job and hotfix decision.
